summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell activation syndrome and recent CABG was admitted for substernal chest pressure and leg cramps. She attributed her symptoms to a mast cell flare, possibly triggered by hypokalemia and stress. Initial evaluation showed a potassium level of 3.0 mEq/L, which was corrected with oral and IV supplementation. Serial troponins were negative, EKGs unchanged, and chest imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. Her symptoms improved with administration of her standard mast cell protocol, including IV Benadryl, Ativan, and Dilaudid. She remained stable on telemetry, with gradual resolution of chest pressure. She was discharged home with potassium supplements and plans for follow-up with her allergist and cardiologist.
problems: Malignant mast cell tumors, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
